cands.name: Dan Weldon
cands.bio: Tampa native and litigation lawyer, former prosecutor; played linebacker at the University of Florida, chaired College Republicans of Florida, UF Levin College of Law graduate. Began 2026 running for Congress (CD 14), switched to HD 64 in June. Won the GOP primary with about 66%.

record.text: No elected office. Ran for Congress in CD 14 against Kathy Castor before switching to HD 64 in June 2026; White House recognized his campus free-speech work in 2019 (per Florida Politics). Priorities: housing, groceries, insurance and energy costs.

money_notes.text: Through Oct. 16 he reported more than $140,000 raised and about $16,500 on hand. The Florida House Republican Campaign Committee gave $40,000 cash plus about $80,500 in staffing, consulting, research and polling. His committee Weldon for Florida raised about $53,000; its largest gift was nearly $36,000 from the Florida Federation for Children.

In June, $10,000 of his $11,000 haul came from 10 political committees giving $1,000 each from the same Tallahassee address, all sharing treasurer Noreen Fenner (who also handles finances for the Florida House Republican Campaign Committee).

endorsements.text: Florida Medical Association PAC (FMA PAC) endorsed him in the primary.

cands.gaps: No newspaper editorial endorsement found. Photo not found (campaign site blocked automated access). Social accounts not found. Owner-source search (Stew Peters / Alex Jones / Owen Shroyer) was NOT run: the shared web-search budget was exhausted, so no owner-source status is known.

cands.name: Luis Salazar
cands.bio: Navy veteran, community organizer and first-generation college graduate with a media/communications background; former president of the Hillsborough Democratic Party LGBTQ+ Caucus. Originally from California, raised in Arizona. Won the 3-way Democratic primary with about 45%.
cands.local_ties: Hillsborough County (Tampa). Florida Politics reports he is originally from California and was raised in Arizona; length of Tampa residency not stated.

record.text: No elected office held. Former president of the Hillsborough County Democratic Party's LGBTQ+ Caucus; works on LGBTQ+ and Latino voter outreach. Platform: stricter insurance-industry oversight, rate-increase justification, storm mitigation.

money_notes.text: Through Oct. 2 he raised about $89,000 and had about $10,000 on hand. Contributors include the Florida AFL-CIO COPE Fund, Everytown for Gun Safety Action Fund, Get Moving Florida PC and a plumbers and pipefitters union ($1,000 each) and Hillsborough CTA-PAC ($500). Affiliated committee Get Moving Florida PC raised about $53,000, including $5,000 from Equality Florida Action PAC.

In the primary, Social Justice PAC (funded by a $100,000 transfer from Greater Florida Foundation, which had received about $2.5 million from eight Republican-aligned committees) mailed pieces promoting Salazar and attacking Mike Suarez. Florida Politics says the filings do not show coordination with Salazar's campaign.

controversies.text: Florida Politics reports court records show a DUI conviction in Las Vegas (2006), a guilty plea to DUI in Flagstaff, Arizona (2013), and a 2015 Hillsborough DUI arrest in which an affidavit says breath samples read 0.200 and 0.210 and he drove away after an officer took his keys. The disposition of the 2015 case was not stated in the article. He did not comment to Florida Politics.

endorsements.text: Sen. Brian Nathan, Rep. Mitch Rosenwald, Sen. Carlos Guillermo Smith, West Central Florida Labor Council AFL-CIO, Ironworkers Local 397, LGBTQ+ Victory Fund.
Equality Florida Action PAC; Hillsborough County LGBTQ+ Democratic Caucus.
Florida Realtors PAC endorsed him in HD 64.
